title: A nil that isn't nil
hints: An interface value is nil only when it holds no type and no value. A nil *Circle stored in a Shape is a non-nil Shape: it has a type.
Find declares var c *Circle and returns it as a Shape. When nothing matches, the Shape it returns holds (*Circle)(nil), which compares unequal to nil.
Return nil directly when there is no match, for example: if name != "circle" { return nil }; return &Circle{Radius: 1}.
